title: A link that repeats a join key is refused locally, by name of the parameter it repeats
notes: The rule: `room`, `token`, `k` and `h` each appear at most once, in either form, and a receiver **MUST NOT** take a value by the order it appears (§5.1). The page link `https://host/?room=…&token=…#k=…&h=…` has no server in it — the receiver derives the connection URL from it — so a repeat there, and a repeat in the fragment, are refused by the client itself, locally and before it opens a socket; the refusal names the parameter it repeats, and `expectRefusal` asserts that naming and not the sentence, because §5.1 leaves the sentence to the client. A repeat in the `wss://…/session?…` form is the server's refusal and is pinned on the wire by `vectors/037`. The refused legs are also the evidence that none of them seated anything: a subject left in a session after one would report itself seated for the next `start`. The last leg is the control — the whole link, which must join — because the other way to pass a corpus of refusals is to refuse everything, and the refusals above differ only in which parameter they must name. The failure this prevents is the one a rewrite that chose a value would ship: one link joining two different rooms in two clients, decided by the order its query was written in.
